correctness.rationale: For any displacement d, cyclic telescoping gives ||f-shift_d f||_1 <= min(d,n-d)V(f); convexity proves the arbitrary-kernel bound. Balanced arc indicators of floor(n/2) and ceil(n/2) selected sites have exactly min(d,n-d) crossings for every displacement, so attain the sharp constant simultaneously. Under full support, equality at displacement floor(n/2) yields 2r floor(n/2)<=n, hence r=1 boundary pair and balanced size; strict residual signs on nested superlevel sets prove two-level uniqueness. The cycle-distance second-difference identity gives explicitly nonnegative Fourier coefficients in the exact heat finite sum, so all derivative signs follow. Unnormalized generator, endpoint t=0, quantifiers and kernel positivity verified. Exact-integer and independent matrix-exponential checks passed; finite experiments are not claimed to prove infinite dimensions.

value.rationale: The exact worst-case counting-vertex-l1 distortion per unit adjacent edge variation is a natural sharp approximation invariant of periodic filters. The full arbitrary-probability-kernel formula converts it to expected geodesic displacement, immediately allowing quantitative comparison and design of nonsymmetric cyclic smoothers; all-order equality rigidity identifies genuine worst-case discontinuities. The continuous-time heat specialization has strictly alternating time derivatives and a positive finite spectral measure, stronger than monotonicity and useful for temporal error budgeting. The result spans all cycle lengths and all cyclic Markov kernels rather than a motivated finite slice or a routine isolated computation.
